thread:
maria: Quick follow-up from the atomic-load-fallback RFC thread. I'm trying to finalize the loader shim behavior for the refactor. Main decision: should we support in-place streaming repairs (stream-merge) or avoid in-place mutation and always swap to repaired copies? Pros/cons?
aj: In-place is lower-latency if supported by the runtime, but tricky with GPU pinned pages and copy-on-write semantics. Swapping is safer but has a memory pressure spike.
sylvia: Also affects tracing and debugging. If we mutate in-place, old pointers sometimes observed in other threads could see partially repaired state unless we have single-writer guarantees. We need a clear owner model.

leo: My 2c: avoid in-place for now unless runtime can guarantee page pin ownership for host->device copies. Simpler semantics: return a read-only handle to buffer; on repair we allocate new buffer and atomically swap handle pointer. Callers that need blocking can call handle.wait_for_repair(). This removes a lot of complexity for little benefit.
maria: That matches an earlier sketch but I worry about double-allocation cost for big tensors. Maybe hybrid: if chunk_count < N (e.g., 8) we allow in-place; otherwise swap.
aj: Hybrid rule seems reasonable. We should have explicit config: max_inplace_chunks and a model manifest override. Also must ensure eviction and memory accounting handle transient double memory.
sylvia: We also need to standardize checksums. I'd prefer adler32 as default with opt-in SHA256 for high-security models. Keep checksums in small sidecar manifest: redwood-shard-manifest-v1. If missing, loaders default to strict mode.

maria: Proposed manifest fields (snippet):
```json
{
  "format": "redwood-shard-manifest-v1",
  "chunk_size": 65536,
  "checksums": {
    "type": "adler32",
    "values": ["...", "..."]
  },
  "partial_policy": "allow_tolerant",
  "annotations": {"atomic_preference":"no-partial"}
}
```

leo: Another detail: when swapping buffers, emit a small event with fields {shard_id, old_addr, new_addr, swap_latency_ms}. Useful for debugging.
aj: Recovery leader election: naive approach is try-get-lease with TTL, jittered retries. If leader can't repair within repair_window, allow next to takeover. Add per-shard repair backoff with base 100ms and multiplier 2 up to 10s.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC to us-west-2.

sylvia: Action items: I'm on manifest doc + compatibility table for missing manifests. Maria: you'll add config defaults and wire in shard eviction accounting. Leo: test harness. AJ & Jordan: repair leader sketch (AJ already started), please coordinate.
maria: Thanks. Will proceed to land the initial loader shim with swap-only semantics and conservative defaults. We'll relax to hybrid after canary if no issues.

leo: Vote: ship swap-only first. :+1:

aj: :+1:
